title: SignalDefinition
$comment: Describes a signal and its fields. Source: mmarkets.excalidraw 'Signals Schema'.

approximate_interval.description: e.g. '20s'. Cadence hint, not a guarantee.

staleness_bound.description: Duration, e.g. '60s'. The maximum age a value may reach before subscribers must treat it as stale. Age is measured in AVAILABILITY-TIME -- the stamp assigned when the value entered the system -- against the triggering event's availability-time; never venue timestamps (cross-feed skew makes them incomparable), never wall clock (nondeterministic under replay). This is a freshness contract the producer commits to, not a cadence estimate (contrast approximate_interval, which is only a hint). How a strategy reacts when a value exceeds this bound is the subscriber's half of the mechanism: strategy-schema signals[].staleness_policy.

variants.description: Required when type='enum'; invalid otherwise (enforced structurally).

location.description: Origin of the field's data. 'internal' = first-party, generated by our own exchange/engine (own book, fills, platform-computed signals). 'external' = ingested from an outside venue or provider (e.g. Pinnacle lines, Chainlink feeds, Binance ticks, Sportradar events). 'private' = a user-defined feed scoped to the author's own account/strategy (model scores, regime flags, offline-learned coefficients streamed in). All three are recorded, versioned, and sequenced identically; location only affects provenance and access scope.

label.description: Human-readable label for a card showing this field. Presentation only: the exchange registry reads it, processors never do.

histogram_hints.$comment: RESERVED — from the whiteboard's '(optional histogram hints?)'. Shape TBD.
